exercise.name: Stability Ball Crunch
steps: Lie back on a gym ball so it supports your lower back, feet wide.
Cross your arms on your chest and curl your shoulders up.
Lower slowly back over the ball until you feel a stretch.
exercise.one_line_summary: Lying back on a 60 cm stability ball with the ball under the lower back, feet flat and wide, arms crossed on the chest. Start arched back over the ball (spine -30 deg); end shoulders curled up (spine +28 deg, pelvis tipped back 10 deg), lower back stays on the ball. Abs are the target.

setup.target: Ball under the lower back, hips just below the top of the ball.
setup.tolerance: ball under the low back, not the shoulder blades
setup.why: S1: with the ball under the lower back, abdominal EMG was about double the shoulder-blade position and above a floor crunch. Library step 1.

setup.target: Arms crossed on the chest, fists on the chest.
setup.tolerance: forearms on the chest, not pulling the head
setup.why: Library step 2 (sit-up); crossed arms keep the hands off the neck.

movement.end: +28 deg (shoulders up, shoulder-hip line ~40 deg above level)
movement.path: Arches back to a stretch, then curls up (library step 3).

muscles.emg: Upper and lower RA higher than a floor crunch with the ball under the low back (S1).
muscles.role: Main mover: curls the rib cage up from the stretch.
muscles.surface: The two vertical bands down the front of the belly, lower ribs to the pubic bone.

muscles.emg: External oblique raised with the ball low (S1); balls raise core EMG (S2).
muscles.role: Keeps the body balanced on the ball; not lit.
muscles.surface: Sides of the waist from the lower ribs to the hip bone.

sources.citation: Sternlicht E, Rugg S, Fujii LL, Tomomitsu KF, Seki MM. 2007. Electromyographic comparison of a stability ball crunch with a traditional crunch. J Strength Cond Res 21(2):506-509. doi:10.1519/R-20436.1
sources.what_it_gave: Ball under the lower back (SB-low): upper/lower rectus abdominis and external oblique higher than a floor crunch, about double the ball-under-shoulder-blades position.

sources.citation: Oliva-Lozano JM, Muyor JM. 2020. Core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review. Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306. doi:10.3390/ijerph17124306
sources.what_it_gave: Erector spinae highest in back extensions (~63% MVIC on the floor, ~56% on a bench); V-sits ~80% MVIC rectus abdominis; adding a stability ball raises core EMG; sit-ups and curl-ups the classic core exercises.
The steps the app shows; the pictures must match them.

clip_check.check: Low back on the ball in both
